summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for acute on chronic diastolic heart failure, presenting with shortness of breath, bilateral leg pain, and low hemoglobin. She was treated with furosemide for fluid overload and received two units of packed red blood cells for anemia of chronic kidney disease. Her mental status improved with dose reduction of sedating medications, resolving toxic-metabolic encephalopathy. Imaging showed no deep vein thrombosis, stable orthopedic hardware, and mild pulmonary congestion. She was discharged home with improved symptoms, a revised medication plan including darbepoetin, and arrangements for home medication support. Follow-up was arranged for breast swelling evaluation and occupational therapy for cognitive and medication safety.
